newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African unions say want to settle sugar strike.
newsitem.headline: S.African unions say want to settle sugar strike.

text.p: Unions representing around 4,000 South African sugar industry workers who have been on a wage strike for two weeks said on Tuesday that the strike was becoming too costly and they wanted to settle.
Workers at 14 mills and refineries, operated by Illovo Sugar Ltd and Tongaat-Hulett Ltd in the KwaZulu-Natal sugarcane belt, have been on strike since July 2.
Union spokesman Eric Botha said the strike had gone on too long and the strikers were losing too much pay.
"The guys have lost too much pay and they can't afford to go on longer, we must finalise this thing," Botha told Reuters.
"I can't see us walking out of negotiations today (Tuesday) without settling. I am sure that by Wednesday, or Thursday at the latest, the strike will be resolved," he added.
A spokesman representing Illovo and Tongaat-Hulett said the companies had offered 11.5 percent backdated to June 1, and an additional increase of two percent in October.
Botha said the five unions representing the workers wanted the increase to be backdated to April 1.
"We might settle for a middle ground of May 1."

The sugar industry has estimated that it was losing some 83,500 tonnes of cane daily in production through the labour action but officials said the blow has been softened somewhat by the early warning of impending strike action by the unions.
An industry source said the unions gave notice six days before the strike of their intention to strike.
Millers were able to notify sugar growers not to deliver cane to the mills, the source said, adding that cane on the fields would only lose some sucrose content.
He said the loss in production could be made up by extending the crushing season -- which ususally runs from the beginning of April to just after Christmas.
